decisions.summary: Extract workspace stack provisioning into a single shared helper `provisionWorkspaceStack()` in `src/lib/workspace/provision-stack.ts`. Both the CLI `pan workspace rebuild`, the new dashboard SSE Start route, and the existing non-streaming POST /api/agents path go through this one helper.

Dashboard Start uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) over a new POST /api/agents/start-stream endpoint. Mirrors the existing POST /api/issues/:id/start-planning pattern (fetch with streaming body, `data: {type, step, total, label, detail, status}\n\n` events) rather than introducing a new WebSocket/RPC channel.

Keep the non-streaming POST /api/agents endpoint working unchanged for Cloister auto-resume, host-override retries, and CLI callers. It will also invoke `provisionWorkspaceStack()` before the stack-health gate so non-dashboard paths self-heal, but without streaming.

Serialize concurrent provisioning with a per-issue async mutex plus a global concurrency cap of 2 simultaneous `docker compose up` runs. Prevents the stack-up storm the issue body flags as Risk #1 when /all-up triggers multiple Starts in parallel.

Progress is emitted at milestone granularity (worktree, .devcontainer render, compose up, health-poll, agent spawn) — not by tailing docker compose logs line-by-line. Matches the checklist UX in the issue body and avoids a noisy log multiplexer. Compose-log tailing is recorded as a follow-up.

`--host` (CLI) / 'Switch to --host (advanced)' (dialog) bypasses provisioning entirely. The break-glass is preserved unchanged so dashboard hacking and prod-shape-incompatible diagnostic work stay possible.

`provisionWorkspaceStack()` is idempotent: when `getWorkspaceStackHealth()` already returns healthy, it emits a 'stack-already-healthy' progress event and short-circuits without running `docker compose up`. Satisfies the acceptance criterion that healthy stacks skip the provision step.

Provisioning is invoked from the Start path (dashboard + CLI) only — NOT from `assertWorkspaceStackHealthyForSpawn()` which is also used by review/test/ship roles and Cloister auto-resume. Those paths continue to surface the unhealthy-stack error so the human can decide to retry from the dashboard.

All new server-reachable code uses async I/O exclusively (execAsync, fs/promises). No execSync, no readFileSync/writeFileSync. Existing sync calls in `workspaceRebuildCommand` are migrated as part of the extraction since the shared helper is reachable from the dashboard route.

Error states in the dialog offer three explicit recovery actions: 'Retry' (re-run provisioning), 'Force rebuild' (compose down -v then re-render then up), 'Switch to --host (advanced)' (skip provisioning + spawn on host with the existing hostOverrideConfirmation flow). Matches the acceptance criterion verbatim.

hazards.summary: Dashboard server code MUST NOT introduce blocking sync I/O. The current `workspaceRebuildCommand` uses readFileSync/rmSync — these are acceptable in the CLI process but become event-loop hazards once the same logic is reachable from `/api/agents/start-stream`.
hazards.mitigation: When extracting to `provisionWorkspaceStack()`, swap sync calls for fs/promises (rm, readFile) and execAsync. Add a no-execsync lint sweep on the new module.

hazards.summary: First-time `docker compose up --build` can run 60–300s. SSE clients and load balancers may time out on quiet streams.
hazards.mitigation: Emit heartbeat progress events (e.g. 'still bringing up containers — elapsed 30s') every ~10s during long compose-up phases. Set route Content-Type/Cache-Control to the values already used by start-planning. Use a 5-minute hard timeout on the compose-up itself (matches workspaceRebuildCommand).

hazards.summary: Concurrent dashboard Starts (the /all-up flywheel pattern) can race docker network/pool exhaustion if every issue gets a `docker compose up` simultaneously.
hazards.mitigation: Global concurrency cap of 2 in-flight provisionings; further Starts queue. Per-issue mutex prevents duplicate provisions for the same issue if the user double-clicks Start. Mutex released in try/finally.

hazards.summary: PAN-1169 (bun --filter populates .bun cache but never creates top-level node_modules symlinks during init) is a hard prerequisite — the on-start provisioning will fail at the bun-install phase without it.
hazards.mitigation: PAN-1169 must merge before PAN-1191 is enabled in production. Add a note to the vBRIEF's `Problem` narrative and tag a hazard for the work agent to recheck PAN-1169's status before testing the end-to-end Start flow. If PAN-1169 is not yet merged, the work agent should rebase onto main after it lands.

hazards.summary: The single-deacon invariant (`.claude/rules/single-deacon-invariant.md`) forbids mounting `~/.panopticon` into workspace containers. The new provisioning path must not introduce such a mount when re-rendering `.devcontainer/`.
hazards.mitigation: Provisioning re-uses the existing `renderDevcontainer()` from `src/lib/workspace/devcontainer-renderer.ts`, which already respects the no-mount + `PANOPTICON_DISABLE_DEACON=1` rules. Do not bypass that renderer.

hazards.summary: Cloister auto-resume runs without UI, so the SSE flow is unavailable to it. If Cloister tries to resume a stopped work-agent whose stack went away (host reboot, manual `docker compose down`), it will hit the existing stack-health gate and fail without any auto-provisioning.
hazards.mitigation: Out of scope for this issue (per D8). File a follow-up to either invoke `provisionWorkspaceStack` from Cloister auto-resume or surface the unhealthy state through the dashboard. Document the gap in `docs/WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md`.

hazards.summary: Compose logs from the init container are interesting (bun install progress, build output) but emitting them through SSE would invert the milestone-style UI the issue calls for.
hazards.mitigation: Phase 1 ships milestones only. If the user wants live install logs in the modal, file a follow-up: `docker compose logs --follow init` piped to SSE as `type: 'log', line: ...` events under a `verbose: true` flag.

hazards.summary: Acceptance criterion calls out that 'CLI `pan start <id>` runs the same provisioning steps and prints the same step-by-step status to stdout.' The existing CLI uses an ora spinner which only renders one line at a time — the issue body's checklist style implies a multi-line ticker.
hazards.mitigation: Replace the single ora spinner in `pan start` with a small multi-line renderer (mirrors `pan workspace rebuild` but lists each step on its own line with elapsed time). Reuse the same `onProgress` callback shape that the SSE route consumes.

hazards.summary: The `POST /api/agents/start-stream` SSE response can't carry the same JSON error contracts the non-streaming `POST /api/agents` returns (guardrails, host-override-required, codex auth, beads-required, provider health). The dialog needs to handle pre-stream errors AND in-stream errors uniformly.
hazards.mitigation: The new endpoint validates pre-flight conditions before opening the SSE stream and returns the existing JSON error shapes with appropriate HTTP status codes for those failures. Once the stream is open, errors are emitted as `type: 'error'` events with the same `error`/`hint` fields. The dialog distinguishes via `res.ok` (same shape as PlanDialog already does).
